title: AI invoice processing: where AP tools stop and the money leaks
description: 15 AP and invoice-capture tools checked, with prices where they exist. Why reading invoices is solved and exceptions and fraud are not.
summary: AI invoice processing reads a supplier invoice, codes it, matches it to the purchase order and gets it approved and paid[^27][^21]. Reading the invoice now costs cents[^10][^11][^9]. The money is in the one invoice in five that hits an exception[^8][^1], and in the fake ones that ask you to pay a new bank account[^12][^13].
verdict: Reading invoices is now cheap and largely solved[^9][^10]; the money leaks in the exceptions and the fraud. About one invoice in five hits an exception[^8][^1], and fake requests to change a supplier's bank account arrive as invoices[^12][^13]. Let an accounts payable tool such as BILL, Ramp or Tipalti run the inbox, approvals and payments[^5][^6][^7]. Put your effort, and any custom AI, into what the suites miss: exception triage, a hold on any change to bank details, and the e-invoices Germany and France now require[^36][^37][^38][^39]. Benchmark any custom step on 50 of your own invoices first.

pickElse: Under a few hundred invoices a month and already on QuickBooks or Xero: use the bill capture built into your accounting software first[^33][^34].
Many entities, countries or currencies: look at the global suites (Tipalti, Coupa, Basware, Medius). Expect a contract and no list price[^7][^21][^24][^23].
You only need the data out of the invoice, not the workflow: a capture tool (Rossum, Nanonets, Docsumo) or a cloud invoice parser feeds your ERP directly[^29][^30][^31][^10][^11].
You run Microsoft Power Platform: AI Builder has a prebuilt invoice model, limited to 360 calls a minute and 20 MB per file[^35].

rules.name: Germany: B2B e-invoicing
rules.what: All businesses must be able to receive EN 16931 e-invoices since 1 Jan 2025. Larger firms must issue them from 2027 and nearly all from 2028[^36][^37][^42].

rules.name: France: B2B e-invoicing
rules.what: Every business must be able to receive e-invoices; large and mid-size firms must issue them. Small firms issue from 1 Sep 2027[^38][^39].

rules.name: EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA)
rules.what: Member states can require e-invoicing; digital reporting for cross-border B2B starts 1 Jul 2030[^41][^42].

rules.name: United States
rules.what: No federal or state B2B e-invoicing mandate[^43]. A voluntary network, DBNAlliance, grew out of an industry pilot the Federal Reserve supported[^44][^43].

howToTest: Pull 50 recent invoices, including credit notes, multi-page invoices, foreign ones and the worst scans.
Write down the right supplier, number, date, total, tax and PO for each before any tool reads them.
Run each tool on the same set. Count wrong values apart from blanks: a wrong total is worse than a missing one.
Add three test invoices that change a supplier's bank details, and check each tool holds them.
Measure how many invoices go straight through, how many reach your team as exceptions, and the cost per invoice including add-ons.

buyVsBuild.buy: Buy for the workflow: inbox, approvals, payments, ERP sync and an audit trail. Suites already sell all of this[^5][^6][^7], and you do not want to own payments.
buyVsBuild.build: Build only the checks your suite misses: exception triage, fraud holds, odd document types, or coding rules specific to your business. Exceptions still hit about one invoice in five[^8]. These checks sit beside the suite and flag what your AP team should look at; the decision stays with a person.

watchOuts: The price you see is rarely the price you pay. Matching, payments, more entities and ERP sync are often add-ons[^5][^16][^7][^23].

Payment fraud rides on invoices[^12][^13]. The AFP found 74% of US organizations were hit by business email compromise in 2025[^4][^15]. Check any change to bank details with a call to a number you look up yourself[^12].
A tool that reads the subtotal as the total looks right at a glance. In our benchmark, 7 of 10 tools picked the wrong one of two look-alike tables[^9].
E-invoices in Germany and France arrive as structured data, and an ordinary PDF no longer counts[^36][^40]. A tool that only reads PDFs will miss the point and the deadlines[^37][^39].
